They are prone to walking away at round 6 when pushed beyond their purported limits, as seen in the deal that failed at ₹81,556. No specific data exists regarding their behavior during quarter-end months.

playbooks.name: Bharat PCB

In recent deals, they closed one at ₹92,477 after a single round and walked away at round 3 in another instance when pushed beyond their stated final price of ₹89,789. The data does not record specific patterns for quarter-end months.

playbooks.name: Nova Components
playbooks.text: Nova Components frequently employs false scarcity and "final price" claims to pressure buyers, though they can be negotiated down when pushed, as seen when a ₹90,490 claim was proven false before closing at ₹87,224. They previously walked away at round 7 after holding to a ₹87,915 price point, indicating they will abandon deals if pushed beyond their stated limits. The data does not record specific behavioral patterns regarding quarter-end months.

playbooks.name: Apex Circuits
playbooks.text: Apex Circuits consistently employs false "final price" claims in round 2 and fabricated competitor pressure tactics to inflate pricing. In closed deals (February-April 2025), they successfully negotiated to prices like ₹85,819, ₹85,333, and ₹83,957, though they famously walked away at round 6 when pressured further (₹81,556) in January. Quarter-end months like March follow this same pattern of deceptive price posturing, confirming that their "final" claims are unreliable and aimed at securing higher margins.

playbooks.name: Bharat PCB
playbooks.text: Bharat PCB maintains rigid price floors, as evidenced by their truthful claim of ₹89,789 in January, and they consistently walk away during the third round of negotiations. Successful deals closed at ₹92,477 and ₹91,516, whereas aggressive attempts to push past their stated limits during quarter-end months led to lost deals like the one abandoned at ₹90,227. To avoid walk-aways, the recommended strategy is to accept their final offer before reaching the third round.

playbooks.name: Nova Components
playbooks.text: Nova Components consistently uses false "final-price" claims at round 3 and deceptive scarcity pressure tactics to manipulate negotiations. Across closed deals, they typically settle after 6 rounds at prices significantly lower than their initial "final" claims (e.g., closing at ₹87,224–₹88,852), though they walked away at round 7 in January. During quarter-end months like March, they continue these aggressive, dishonest tactics without any observed change in their underlying negotiation pattern.
